<section class="resources-section">

        <h1 class="section-heading">Drake Golf Model Repository</h1>
        <p class="resource-description">
          Golf swing models and simulations implemented using Drake, an open-source toolbox from MIT's Robot 
          Locomotion Group. Focuses on underactuated systems, manipulation, and control-affine dynamics for 
          golf biomechanics analysis.
        </p>
        <div class="site-card site-card--callout u-mb-2">
          <h2 class="u-mb-1">Authority Boundary</h2>
          <p class="resource-description">
            <strong>This establishes</strong> educational overviews and repository links for Drake-based golf swing models in UpstreamDrift.
            Current UpstreamDrift engine support tiers are governed separately on the <a href="../models/programming/engines.html">Engines and Runtime Support</a> catalog.
          </p>
          <p class="resource-description">
            <strong>This does not establish</strong> human validation, clinical applicability, or coaching readiness.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Overview</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          This repository contains golf swing models implemented in Drake, which provides a suite of tools for 
          analyzing the dynamics of robots and building control systems. Drake is designed to provide a flexible 
          and efficient platform for robotics research and development, with capabilities for modeling, simulation, 
          trajectory optimization, and control design. Highly relevant for implementing control-affine systems 
          and analyzing underactuated systems like the golf swing.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Features</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          <strong>Control-Affine Systems:</strong> Native support for control-affine dynamics<br>
          <strong>Underactuated Analysis:</strong> Tools for analyzing underactuated systems<br>
          <strong>Trajectory Optimization:</strong> Optimization tools for swing planning<br>
          <strong>Simulation:</strong> High-fidelity physics simulation<br>
          <strong>Visualization:</strong> Integrated visualization tools
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Repository Access</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          The Drake golf model implementations and simulation scripts are hosted in the UpstreamDrift repository:
          <br><br>
          <a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="resource-link">View on GitHub →<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a>
          <br><br>
          <strong>Clone with Git:</strong><br>
          <code>git clone https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift.git</code>
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Related Resources</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          This repository is closely related to the <a href="../models/models-drake.html">Drake Models page</a>, which 
          includes links to Russ Tedrake's courses (Underactuated Robotics and Robotic Manipulation), installation 
          guides, and comprehensive support resources. Drake is particularly well-suited for control-affine system 
          analysis and underactuated system control, making it ideal for golf swing biomechanics research.
          See the <a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift" target="_blank" rel="noopener">UpstreamDrift repository<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a> for simulation scripts and example setups.
        </p>
      </div>
